purpose: English-only public development candidate extending collaborative autoethnography. Register before acquisition; publication and availability do not establish writing quality or completed reading.

sources.title: Collaborative Autoethnography as a Pathway for Teacher Learning
sources.selection_question: How do two educators connect recollected participation, contrasting personal concerns and changes in teaching or professional identity? Examine the role of collaboration in interpretation rather than treating two first-person narratives as automatic corroboration.
sources.version_note: Publisher open PDF, Volume 5(2), pages 10-21. Verify identity, actual design and license from the article and publisher before analysis. Keep full source outside the public repository.
